bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 131082 in `ZSTD_decodeLiteralsBlock()` while `simple_decompress` was processing a legacy zstd v0.3 frame. The staged 131102-byte witness begins with four libFuzzer seed bytes, then a legacy-frame magic `23 b5 2f fd`, a compressed-block header `12 00 10`, and a raw-literals header `29 00 08`. `ZSTD_getcBlockSize()` decodes the block header as `cBlockSize = 131088` and `bt_compressed`, and the raw-literals header decodes as `litSize = 131082`. Because `litSize > srcSize - 11`, `ZSTD_decodeLiteralsBlock()` takes the fallback path that copies raw literals into `dctx->litBuffer`; however, the vulnerable code only rejects `litSize > srcSize - 3` and never enforces the patch's missing `litSize <= BLOCKSIZE` requirement. For the witness, `131082 <= 131085`, so `memcpy(dctx->litBuffer, istart, litSize)` writes 131082 bytes into `litBuffer[BLOCKSIZE + 8]`, a 131080-byte array inside stack `ZSTD_DCtx ctx`, overflowing the decoder context by 2 bytes and matching the saved ASan report.

source.description: First project-code read of the attacker-controlled compressed stream on the witnessed path: it loads the frame magic that decides whether zstd will dispatch into the legacy decoder family.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 131102 bytes long. `simple_decompress` first hashes and strips the first four bytes `20 20 20 20` with `FUZZ_seed()`, so project code receives the remaining 131098 bytes starting `23 b5 2f fd`. This statement materializes that attacker-controlled 32-bit prefix as `magicNumberLE = 0xFD2FB523`, which `ZSTD_isLegacy()` maps to legacy version 3.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The raw-literals sub-block header is decoded into the copy length used by the later guards and the overflowing `memcpy()`. For the witness bytes `29 00 08`, this expression yields `litSize = 131082`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The fallback raw-literals path copies the attacker-derived `litSize` bytes into the fixed `litBuffer` scratch array embedded in the stack decoder context.
sink.note: For the witness, `litSize` is 131082 while `dctx->litBuffer` is `BLOCKSIZE + 8 = 131080` bytes. ASan reports `WRITE of size 131082` at this line and identifies stack `ctx` in `ZSTD_decompress()` as the overrun object.

root_cause.description: In the `IS_RAW` fallback copy path, the vulnerable decoder validates only that the literals fit in the remaining input bytes. It never checks that `litSize` also fits in `dctx->litBuffer` before copying into that fixed `BLOCKSIZE + 8` array.
root_cause.note: The witness satisfies the existing input-length guard because `131082 <= 131085`, so execution falls through to the copy. The fixing patch inserts the missing `litSize > BLOCKSIZE` rejection immediately before this line.

parser_admitted.condition: After `FUZZ_seed()` strips the first four bytes, the witness begins with legacy magic `23 b5 2f fd`, so `ZSTD_isLegacy(src, srcSize)` returns 3 and `ZSTD_decompressMultiFrame()` enters the legacy decoder branch instead of normal zstd frame parsing.

fine_trace.note: Reads the first four bytes of the attacker-controlled stream seen by project code and materializes them as `0xFD2FB523`. The subsequent `switch(magicNumberLE)` maps that exact value to legacy decoder version 3, making the v0.3 code path reachable.

Because step 1 yields a supported legacy magic, `ZSTD_decompressMultiFrame()` takes the legacy branch and `ZSTD_decompressLegacy()` routes the witness into `ZSTDv03_decompress()` instead of the regular frame decoder.

The legacy one-shot decompressor allocates stack decoder context `ctx`. That context contains `litBuffer[BLOCKSIZE + 8]`, a fixed 131080-byte scratch array; ASan later names this stack object as the overrun destination.

Parses the first v0.3 block header bytes `12 00 10` into `headerFlags = 0x12`, `cSize = 131088`, and `blockType = bt_compressed`. That attacker-derived `cSize` becomes the `srcSize` argument passed into `ZSTD_decodeLiteralsBlock()` for this block.
The first byte of the literals sub-block is `0x29`, so `*istart & 3` is `1` and the decoder takes `case IS_RAW` instead of the compressed-literals or RLE-literals handlers.

Decodes the raw-literals size from the first three header bytes of the literals block. For the witness bytes `29 00 08`, the 24-bit field yields `litSize = 131082`, which is later reused both in the fallback guards and as the `memcpy()` byte count.

With `srcSize = 131088` from step 4, the witness satisfies `131082 > 131077`, so the decoder enters the local-buffer fallback path instead of directly referencing `istart + 3`. The block then has only 3 bytes left after `litSize + 3`, which is why the fallback path is taken.

This fallback path checks only that the requested copy stays within the remaining input bytes. For the witness, `131082 <= 131085`, so the function does not reject it even though the destination from step 3 is only `BLOCKSIZE + 8 = 131080` bytes. The vulnerable code has no `litSize > BLOCKSIZE` guard here.

Sink. The copy uses the attacker-derived `litSize = 131082` from step 6 against the fixed `litBuffer` from step 3, so it writes 2 bytes past the 131080-byte array and overflows stack `ctx`. ASan reports `WRITE of size 131082` at this line with `ZSTD_decompress -> ZSTD_decompressDCtx -> ZSTD_decompressBlock` beneath it.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: ASan reports the crashing write at fine-trace step 9, `memcpy(dctx->litBuffer, istart, litSize)` in `ZSTD_decodeLiteralsBlock()`.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan names stack `ctx` in `ZSTD_decompress()` as the overrun object. Fine-trace step 3 identifies `ctx.litBuffer` as the fixed destination, and step 8 shows the missing `BLOCKSIZE` guard that lets `litSize` exceed that destination.

format.contract: The verified witness is the staged 131102-byte libFuzzer file consumed by `simple_decompress`. Its first four bytes `20 20 20 20` are harness seed material removed by `FUZZ_seed()`. The remaining 131098 bytes begin with legacy zstd v0.3 magic `23 b5 2f fd`, then block header `12 00 10`, then raw-literals header `29 00 08`. Those exact staged bytes make `ZSTD_getcBlockSize()` derive `cBlockSize = 131088` and `ZSTD_decodeLiteralsBlock()` derive `litSize = 131082`, so the raw-literals fallback takes the `litSize > srcSize-11` branch but not the `litSize > srcSize-3` rejection. The resulting `memcpy(dctx->litBuffer, istart, litSize)` copies 131082 bytes into the 131080-byte `litBuffer` and reproduces the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow write.
